verses.text: The three men stopped answering Job because he was convinced he was in the right.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, got angry with Job for defending himself instead of defending God.
He was also angry with Job’s three friends because they had condemned Job even though they had found no answer for him.
Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he was.
When Elihu saw that the three men had nothing left to say, he got angry.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite said, “I’m young, and you’re much older. So I held back and didn’t dare tell you what I thought.
I thought, ‘Age should have its say. A long life should teach wisdom.’
But it’s the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.
Being important doesn’t make a person wise, and being old doesn’t guarantee they understand justice.
So I said, ‘Listen to me. I’ll tell you what I think too.’
I waited to hear what you had to say. I listened to your reasoning as you searched for the right words.
I gave you my full attention. None of you proved Job wrong or answered what he said.
Don’t say, ‘We’ve found wisdom. Only God can prove him wrong.’
Job hasn’t aimed his words at me, and I won’t answer him with the speeches you gave.
They’re stunned and have stopped answering. They don’t have a word to say.
Should I keep waiting because they won’t speak, because they just stand there with no answer?
I’ll give my own answer and say what I think.
I have plenty to say, and the spirit inside me won’t let me hold it in.
I feel like wine sealed tight in a new wineskin that’s about to burst.
I need to speak to get some relief. I’ll open my mouth and answer.
I won’t play favorites or flatter anyone with fancy titles.
I wouldn’t know how to flatter someone. If I did, my Maker would soon take me away.
